text.p: The International Air Services Commission said on Tuesday it had allocated capacity to Qantas Airways Ltd for three years on the Netherlands route.

The commission said in an interim decision that the three-year allocation would allow it to assess how services on that route developed, while allowing Qantas to operate its proposed three flights a week to Amsterdam.
Qantas had applied for capacity for five years, rather than the three years that were granted.
The airline will operate the flights on a code-share basis with British Airways Plc.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways.
"The commission did not find significant tourism, consumer, competition, trade or industry structure benefits arising from the proposal," the commission said in a statement.
"However, the commission decided that an allocation was appropriate given that the use of Australian capacity is in itself regarded as a benefit to the public."
The commission also renewed Qantas' capacity allocations to Papua New Guinea, which were due to expire on June 30, 1997.
